answer: A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, since the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The horizon multiplier is published, charged in summit, and oasis lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 11 for every participant already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival forfeits the most. A farm of 4277 identities would post 2685 proofs and burn roughly 65 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
